scope: personal-adventure

targets.audience: owner; friends only by explicit sharing
targets.story: light premise, regional milestones and clear ending; detailed worldbuilding later

epics.title: Reliable systems and reusable adventure data
Satisfying capture, companion choice and compact battles
Four varied biomes and a light first adventure
Reusable pixel assets and comfortable personal play
Lightweight checks and private playable updates

tasks.title: Define the personal adventure content matrix and first playable target
scope: Record four biomes (meadow, wetland, rocky badlands, snowy forest), two compact maps per biome and 12 species with three associated with each biome. Counts are starting budgets, not incentives to add filler.
Build a content matrix of map purpose, route/challenge, landmarks, species roles, reused assets and regional milestone. Reuse all eight existing species where they fit and add four new designs.

Keep a short-to-medium progression thread and clear ending; 2–4 hours is an initial pacing hypothesis, not a fixed duration or completion gate. Detailed lore, branching narrative, six mandatory side quests and evolutions are deferred.
Use owner enjoyment as the design test. Mature/sensitive themes are allowed, not required; retain the existing tone until a concrete creative choice improves play.
accept: The content matrix has exactly four biome groups, eight distinct map briefs and 12 species slots.
The first meadow pair has a playable objective without requiring a story bible or narrative engine.
Private personal play, optional sharing with friends, direct main integration and reuse boundaries are documented.
tasks.parallel: Ready now. Map sketches, creature concepts, audio/art references and reliability fixes can start alongside this short design task.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: README.md describes a browser prototype; there is no design document, campaign target, content budget, or definition of a finished game.

tasks.title: Fix save crashes and preserve progress while adding stable content IDs
scope: Validate nested team/save data and safely recover corrupted payloads without overwriting the only recoverable checkpoint.
Migrate index-based species/region references to stable IDs before adding wetland maps, new creatures or rearranging pools.
Preserve valid v1/v2 collection, XP, health, inventory and unlocked regions; handle missing/denied storage visibly.
Retain one last-known-good backup rather than building a large save platform.
accept: The team={"0":7} reproduction opens recovery or valid play instead of crashing.
Legacy saves retain progress when IDs/data order change; invalid and future-version data have safe outcomes.
A failed write/migration leaves a usable prior checkpoint.
tasks.parallel: Hotfix immediately. Coordinate stable-ID/save-envelope changes with module and story-pack contracts; no need to wait for new maps.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:20–42 trusts nested team records; a v2 save with team={'0':7} reproduces "Cannot create property xp on number 7" and prevents window.mossvale from initializing. Species/regions are persisted as array indexes.

tasks.title: Separate reusable game systems from content with a small module split
scope: Extract game state/save, input/movement, battle rules, content/asset registry and UI/rendering boundaries from the single IIFE. Format source and CSS readably.
Use stable IDs and injected RNG/time where tests need them. Keep Canvas and vanilla JavaScript unless an actual need justifies a dependency.
Document the few data/event contracts needed for map and adventure packs.
Avoid a general-purpose engine rewrite, visual editor, plugin framework or months of infrastructure. Gate mutable debug helpers to development.
accept: A map/creature/adventure data edit does not require changing movement or battle code.
Existing gameplay/save smoke tests pass through the incremental split.
Separate code/data/asset files give parallel workers clear ownership.
tasks.parallel: Core code owner coordinates shared contracts. Tests, content briefs and art preparation can proceed independently.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js contains rendering, mutation, persistence, DOM menus, combat and content in one 282-line compressed IIFE; dist/style.css is seven very long lines. Shared mutable state makes independent edits conflict.

tasks.title: Add a lightweight local check command and CI smoke checks
scope: Commit reproducible syntax, asset-reference and startup/save smoke checks with simple local instructions.
Add minimal lint/format tooling only where useful; pin any introduced tools.
Run checks on main/branches without requiring PR approvals or mandatory merge reviews.
Keep checks focused on preventing broken builds and lost saves, not commercial certification.
accept: A clean checkout can serve the game and run the documented checks.
Known missing-asset/startup/save failures are detected.
Direct main commits remain possible with visible check results.
tasks.parallel: Ready now; small build/test files are independent of map production.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: The repository contains README plus dist assets only: no package manifest, lockfile, linter, formatter, committed tests or CI workflow. Earlier validation scripts exist only in the task workspace, not the repo.

tasks.title: Preserve encounters through refresh and browser interruptions
scope: Use explicit exploration/battle/result/pause transitions and cancel stale timers.
Implement a safe checkpoint/resume policy: item use, HP, captures and rewards must resolve once across reload.
Suspend/resume consistently when the browser tab hides or mobile is interrupted.
Guard against double taps, double actions and reward duplication.
accept: Refreshing during capture cannot spend an orb and simply discard its action.
Stale callbacks do not affect a new encounter; pause/visibility behavior is predictable.
Defeat, switch and result flows always return to usable play.
tasks.parallel: Requires state/save contracts; map/art and battle design can advance independently.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:203–229 uses setTimeout for turns while battle state is not serialized. Browser reproduction: start capture, reload immediately; orbs drop 12→11 but the encounter disappears. document.hidden only stops loop rendering/simulation, not turn timers.

tasks.title: Detect missing assets and recover startup failures
scope: Use named asset IDs with required/optional classification and loading status.
Provide retry/error feedback for required missing sprites; optional audio/font failures remain nonfatal.
Reject malformed manifest references before play or in the asset check.
Reuse the manifest later for biome/creature packs.
accept: Aborting the player sprite shows a deliberate error/retry path, not invisible play.
Slow loading communicates progress and does not accept premature movement.
Optional asset failure does not break the game.
tasks.parallel: Ready now. Manifest conventions coordinate with reusable packs and asset production.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:70 resolves both image.onload and image.onerror identically; aborting sprite8.png still boots with no failure message and an invisible player.

tasks.title: Keep a small deterministic gameplay and save regression suite
scope: Commit tests for saves/migrations, movement, capture, item/reward transactions and regional unlocks.
Use seeded RNG/time fixtures and a few real browser flows rather than mutating live production globals.
Keep a normal-action meadow challenge flow; do not use forced enemy HP as evidence of fun or balance.
Add tests for bugs that could lose progress, block play or invalidate reusable data.
accept: Relevant checks run locally and in CI with reproducible failures.
Duplicate rewards, corrupt saves, missing required assets and stale action callbacks are caught.
At least one normal capture/challenge path works without debug damage.
tasks.parallel: Test scenarios can be prepared now; implementations follow shared state contracts, independently from art/content production.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: No tests are committed. Previous workspace browser scripts forced guardian HP to 1 and Math.random to 0, verifying wiring but not real difficulty, natural navigation or complete playability.

tasks.title: Create a simple validated map and event data format
scope: Define JSON map data for terrain, collision, layers, landmarks, spawn points, exits, encounter zones and simple triggers.

Separate persistent chest/challenge completion from immutable map geometry.

Invalid exits/assets/spawns are detected with useful context.
The format supports eight authored maps and persistent regional milestones.
tasks.parallel: One schema owner; all four map-pair briefs can be drafted in parallel and implemented in separate files after the contract settles.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:49–67 hardcodes one ellipse, central cross-path, pond, grass rules and the same special object positions for all regions. Terrain palettes change, but authored geography and event data do not exist.

tasks.title: Make eight-direction movement, followers and map transitions feel good
scope: Keep consistent eight-direction world movement and collision footprints matching terrain/props.
Handle corner sliding, safe exits/spawns, repeated interact input and stuck recovery.
Preserve zoom through resize; improve camera bounds/occlusion and keep followers off water/obstacles.
Tune walk/run responsiveness from the owner’s actual play feedback.
accept: Every required route and exit is traversable without clipping or trapping the player.
Keyboard/touch directions and movement distance are consistent across ordinary frame rates.
Camera/follower behavior remains readable and zoom survives resize.
tasks.parallel: Core traversal can use fixtures while each biome author works on a separate map file.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:68 checks circular object radii; movement resolves X then Y and follows a fixed camera. resize resets user zoom. The follower uses a fixed offset regardless of obstacles or water.

tasks.title: Make a small set of battle actions meaningfully different
scope: Keep a compact action set: reliable strike, a distinctive creature move, capture, guard, potion and switch.
Give the special move a cost/cooldown or useful tradeoff so it is not simply a stronger unlimited strike.
Use a small shared damage/type/status rule set with clear feedback; add at most a few effects that create real decisions.
Preserve readable capture chances and centralize action resolution.
accept: At least two offensive choices and defensive/switch choices have practical uses.
Displayed effects/chances match actual rules.
A player can learn the system through play without extensive stats or documentation.
tasks.parallel: Rules can be designed alongside maps and roster roles. One battle module owner avoids incompatible mechanics; UI/art use its events.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:203–225 offers one basic strike and one elemental move per species, unlimited elemental attacks, simple guard/potion/switch, and alternating enemy actions. Neutral elemental attack generally outdamages the basic move without a cost.

tasks.title: Keep companion selection and a small active team simple
scope: Retain a collection of owned species and let any captured friend travel with the player.
Support a small three-companion battle team and simple reorder/switch/inspect controls if the first trial confirms it improves decisions.
Define duplicates, full team and all-fainted recovery without building breeding, hidden traits or an individual-creature database.
Preserve current one-record-per-species saves; reserve individual duplicates/nicknames for later only if desired.
accept: Captured friends remain selectable and persist with their XP/health.
Team management and battle switching are clear on the owner’s devices.
Every team can recover from defeat; no capture disappears because the active team is full.
tasks.parallel: Party UI and battle logic can work against the agreed lightweight collection contract.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: save.caught is a species-index set and save.team is one record per species. Duplicate captures yield coins/XP and cannot become distinct companions; there is no limited active party or reserve collection.

tasks.title: Add lightweight milestones and dialogue hooks, not a narrative engine
scope: Data-drive discovery, chest, regional challenge and exit-unlock milestones with once-only rewards.
Provide short optional NPC/sign lines, objective cues and a persisted current goal.
Leave slots for later dialogue/story roles without implementing branching quest graphs or a scripting language.
Keep map/entity names separate from story-specific character roles.
accept: A simple objective/unlock chain is authored as data and resumes correctly.
Rewards/unlocks commit once and required progress cannot softlock.
The owner can follow the next destination without a lore dump.
tasks.parallel: Brief text and map event placement can happen in parallel; milestone IDs/rewards need one coordinating owner.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: objective() derives one hardcoded step from captures/badges; Iris dialogue is repeated HTML. There are no branching dialogue nodes, persistent quest instances or general map events.

tasks.title: Keep supplies and rewards useful without forced grinding
scope: Keep orbs, potions, coins and convenient healing with a small shared item/reward table.
Ensure free recovery prevents dead ends, and choose the refill policy intentionally.
Make purchases/use/rewards transactional with clear feedback.
Tune reward amounts to eight compact maps rather than a commercial economy or long grind loop.
accept: Spending supplies cannot make the adventure unwinnable.
Purchases, chests and battle rewards persist exactly once.
The owner finds rewards useful without feeling compelled to repeat fights for currency.
tasks.parallel: Item/reward tables can be prepared alongside maps; transactions share the save/action service.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: Inventory is three scalar counts. Iris restores health and fills orbs to 12 for free; duplicate catches grant 10 coins; shops have hardcoded prices and two items. These choices have not been economy-tested.

tasks.title: Add quick continue/new-game and only useful settings
scope: Offer immediate continue/new-game with safe restart confirmation.
Persist sound/motion/run/zoom preferences that are actually useful to the owner.
Keep pause/settings/navigation coherent on keyboard and touch.
Do not add account screens, profile customization or feature-heavy menu infrastructure.
accept: Existing saves resume promptly; starting over cannot silently erase recoverable progress.
Useful preferences persist through reload.
Main controls fit the owner’s normal screens.
tasks.parallel: Layouts can be prepared now; a small UI owner coordinates focus/navigation primitives.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: index.html opens straight into play; there is no title/new-game/continue flow. Sound starts off each time, zoom resets on resize, and other settings do not persist.

tasks.title: Add a portable save backup and simple restore
scope: Provide one validated JSON export/import and restore-from-last-good checkpoint.
Show a concise progress preview before import/overwrite.
Explain that saves are local to the browser/origin; avoid account/cloud dependence.
Multiple named slots and cloud synchronization are not required.
accept: Progress transfers between the owner’s supported browsers by export/import.
Invalid/future-version imports do not overwrite valid progress.
Restore is usable without developer tools.
tasks.parallel: Independent of map production once the save format is stable.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: The only save is localStorage on one browser origin. There is no export/import, checkpoint restore, named slot or user recovery; hosted and localhost progress cannot transfer.

tasks.title: Create 12 useful creatures, three associated with each biome
scope: Reuse the eight existing creatures where they fit and create four additional species to reach 12 total.
Assign three primary inhabitants per biome with distinct silhouettes, personalities, battle roles and encounter hints.
Use the shared asset manifest/pixel anchors and data-driven move/stat/habitat definitions.
Avoid mandatory evolution trees, hidden traits, duplicate-instance genetics and a 24-species production target.
accept: Exactly 12 initial species are available, with three primary associations per biome and no required collection lockout.
Each creature is visually distinct and has a useful role beyond recoloring.
Definitions, art references and availability pass validation.
tasks.parallel: Creature briefs/data and art can be batched by biome after shared style/IDs; one gameplay owner reviews the role matrix for overlap.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: The issue #24 branch defines 12 stable-ID species with three primary residents in each of four biomes, individual battle stats/moves, documented personalities and field hints, and four new transparent sprites. One representative map per biome exposes its primary residents; the second map per biome remains tracked separately.

tasks.title: Tune modest XP growth and small move upgrades
scope: Keep a bounded level/XP curve and simple health/strength growth suitable for a short adventure.
Allow a small move upgrade/choice only if it adds enjoyable progression.
Prevent unused companions becoming useless and avoid obligatory leveling grind.
Evolution lines and elaborate learnsets remain outside the first adventure.
accept: Progression gives satisfying rewards without inflating difficulty or requiring repeated fights.
Switching to a newly caught creature remains viable.
Old XP/level values migrate safely and growth cannot overflow.
tasks.parallel: Tables can be drafted alongside roster design; final tuning follows personal play sessions, not a large simulation program.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:43 and 133 use an unbounded linear level formula, fixed XP per outcome and HP increases. There are no learnsets, level cap or evolutions.

tasks.title: Pace encounters by biome and make creature discovery readable
scope: Use encounter zones/pools appropriate to each compact map and biome, with deliberate weights and level ranges.
Keep a grace period and allow exploration without excessive interruption.
Expose practical habitat hints and guarantee every required creature has an accessible source.
Add a small scripted encounter only where it makes exploration more interesting.
accept: The four biomes have meaningfully different encounters and all 12 species can be found.
Travel and backtracking are not a stream of unavoidable battles.
Encounters and cooldowns behave correctly through save/restore and map transitions.
tasks.parallel: Independent encounter data files can be tuned alongside biome maps once roster and battle contracts are stable.
tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:190–195 uses region-wide pools and a preference for unseen species; movement accumulates a grass-distance threshold. There are no zone-specific habitats, trainer events or encounter protection items.

tasks.title: Make four regional challenges feel different without complex AI
scope: Create one compact challenge per biome, using existing creatures or small teams with a distinct tactic or environmental setup.

Allow healing/retry and alternate team strategies.
Do not require extra boss-species art or an additional final boss; the finale can be a destination/completion moment.
accept: Four regional challenges test different useful decisions.
Each can be completed with more than one sensible team/strategy.
Losing/retrying never blocks progress or duplicates rewards.

tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.

tasks.title: Integrate and validate the four biome map pairs
scope: Integrate the four linked biome packages: eight compact authored maps total. This issue covers shared integration, not duplicate production estimates.
Check exits/unlocks, spawns, required landmarks, return routes and discovery tracking across all map pairs.
Keep geography and atmosphere distinct, with at least one different exploration activity in each biome.
Record a map/asset reuse inventory and avoid repeating one geometry with palette swaps.

Each biome is recognizable from its layout and activity as well as its artwork.

tasks.title: Connect the adventure with a light premise and clear ending
scope: Use short goals/dialogue to connect exploration and four regional milestones to one clear final destination.
Add brief playable hints for capture, healing and switching; no lengthy tutorial cutscene.
Persist adventure completion and allow continued roaming/collecting afterward.
Defer detailed lore, branching narratives, extensive character arcs and controversial themes unless a concrete choice is enjoyable.
accept: The owner understands why to move onward and recognizes when the adventure is complete.

After the ending, uncollected creatures and maps remain available.

tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.

Let the owner’s taste override nominal map/creature counts or duration when a change improves the game.

Reported frustrations are fixed, deliberately retained or documented as a later preference.
The final loop is enjoyable to the owner without debug intervention or obligatory grind.

tasks.verify: Run relevant gameplay/save regressions and try the changed experience in a normal playable build.

tasks.title: Make objectives, team selection and battle information easy to use

tasks.title: Separate reusable asset/system definitions from adventure packs
scope: Define an adventure pack containing maps, species availability, object/NPC roles, brief text, milestone order and ending references.
Resolve visual assets through a shared manifest and stable IDs; changing an NPC role or cottage purpose must not require new artwork or copied game systems.
Namespace persistent adventure/map/entity flags so later stories do not collide with existing saves.
Prove reuse with two tiny fixture scenes that assign different roles/text to the same building/character assets; do not write a second full story yet.
accept: The first adventure is content data on top of shared movement/battle/save systems.
The reuse fixtures swap scene roles while reusing the same assets and mechanics.
Broken references and incompatible pack/save IDs fail validation; no first-adventure progress is corrupted.
tasks.parallel: One owner freezes registry/pack/save contracts. Once stable, each biome and creature pack is independently authorable.
tasks.verify: Validate pack references and load both small fixtures; verify scene roles change while engine code/assets remain the same.
tasks.evidence: New scoped requirement from the personal-use, varied-biome, reusable-asset direction.

tasks.title: Build the meadow biome pack with two distinct compact maps
scope: Author two compact maps: a sunlit trail and a ruined orchard. These are working briefs, not fixed lore; adjust geometry to the owner’s enjoyment.
Use winding footpaths, tree cover and a hidden shortcut so the biome differs in play, not only palette.
Produce/reuse a coherent terrain/prop/landmark asset batch using the shared manifest and source/export conventions.
Place three associated creatures, an accessible supply/recovery point, optional discoveries and one regional challenge/milestone. Wire safe entry, return and onward exits.
Keep dialogue brief and assign story roles through adventure data so these maps/assets can support future stories.
accept: Both maps have distinct geometry and a useful exploration/challenge purpose.
Required creatures, milestone, exits and return routes are reachable and validated.
The biome asset/data pack is reusable and visually coherent with the player/creatures.

deferred.title: Add six side quests, regional secrets and collection goals
deferred.reason: Detailed side quests, regional lore and branching narrative are postponed until after the first varied personal adventure. Small discoveries belong in the biome packages, not a mandatory six-quest campaign.

deferred.title: Document code, artwork, audio and font rights for distribution
deferred.reason: A formal public/commercial distribution rights review is not a delivery gate for this personal project. Ordinary asset/source metadata remains part of reusable asset work; no blanket claim of copyright exemption is being made.

deferred.title: Add bounded diagnostics, feedback and support information
deferred.reason: Public support, telemetry and a formal feedback/diagnostic service are not needed for one owner. Useful local errors and reproduction notes stay in the lightweight check/save tasks.

deferred.title: Evaluate opt-in cloud saves and cross-device accounts
deferred.reason: Local saves plus export/restore cover current personal use. Accounts/cloud sync are deferred.

deferred.title: Evaluate trading or PvP as a separate online product track
deferred.reason: Trading/PvP, servers, competitive authority and public online operations are outside the agreed adventure.

deferred.title: Expand postgame with rematches, challenge routes and new regions
deferred.reason: Additional regions, rematch systems and a new story are deferred until the first four-biome adventure is enjoyable. Reusable pack support is retained now.

deferred.title: Evaluate installable offline play and safe service-worker updates
deferred.reason: PWA installation/service workers are optional later work. A normal browser game is the current target.

deferred.title: Evaluate translations, controller input and additional platform ports
deferred.reason: Translation, controller support and native ports are not needed until the owner wants those specific capabilities.
